# The shell's answers on the mutation corpus (internal/judge/corpus_test.go), one line a case, in the corpus's
# order: "<exit> <verdict.json> <verdict.md> <stdout> <case>", each the first 16 hex of its sha256, or - when the
# judge wrote none or printed nothing; stdout with the run directory's path as "<dir>". A case is "<base> <edit>":
# judging is g20261018-075357 and recording is g20261017-172556, both judged as v2; v1 is g20261014-215905. The
# archived shell judges wrote these lines, run with bash and jq 1.7.x; TestCorpusAnswers holds Go's answers to them.
# testdata/shell-corpus-v3.txt holds each case again, judged under v3.
#
# Triage. 1461 cases: 1001 judging, 75 recording, 385 v1. The shell exits 0 on 359, 1 on 997 and 2 on 105, and
# writes 831 distinct verdict.json and 665 distinct verdict.md; 115 cases leave their base's verdict.json as it was.
# Go and the shell agree on every case, exit, stdout and both files: 0 differences. The rules needed no change to get
# there. The reader needed one, found in review: a NUL byte ends a number token, as in jq (internal/jsonx/read.go;
# the 5 cases with \x00 in their names). 52 of the 105 exits 2 are an input file that is a directory or cannot be
# read: load() prints "unreadable" twice there, the gathered input does not parse, and both judges stop
# (internal/judge/input.go). v3 brought 5 cases whose readings sit a hair below the incumbent's, so a d rounds to -0
# (the last 4 judging cases and the last recording case but one).
#
# Kept out of the corpus, each for a cause outside the judge's rules. Go and the shell differ on the first two, 11
# cases, under v2 and under v3 alike. The shell answers on the edit as jq reads it, and Go on the edit as Gather
# reads it.
#   - Number spellings jq 1.7 reads and RFC 8259 does not (01, -01, 1., .5, +1, 1.e5, Infinity, nan; 10 cases): the
#     reader refuses them on purpose (internal/jsonx/read.go; TestReaderDifferences), so the file is "unreadable" in
#     Go and read in jq. jq or yq wrote every input a gate run holds.
#   - An item directory whose name is not UTF-8 (1 case): an fs.FS cannot open it (fs.ValidPath), so Gather fails
#     where the shell reads the name as U+FFFD (internal/judge/input.go). No committed run holds one.
#   - The 28 permission edits (a file, or an item directory, its mode set so it cannot be read) when the test runs
#     as root, who reads it whatever its mode: TestCorpusAnswers skips those cases then.
